spaces.title: The Astor Place Workaround

spaceQuestion.text: Your train is dead at Astor Place and you're already late — walk it, bus it, or eat the $34 car? Defend your choice.

spaces.whyNow: An early-morning train fire at Astor Place injured a dozen and left the 6 line limping all week, so half of downtown is improvising a commute right now.

critique.note: Title reads like a Netflix doc. Kept the premise — the commute-improv question is genuinely good.
critique.originalQuestion: Your train is dead at Astor Place and you're already late — do you walk it, bus it, or spend $34 on a car, and what does that choice say about you?

spaces.title: Park Ave With No Cars

spaceQuestion.text: Park Avenue is car-free for exactly seven hours — talk me through your ideal route, including the stop you'd make that has nothing to do with exercise.

spaces.whyNow: Summer Streets is handing New Yorkers a car-free Park Avenue again this weekend, the one morning a year the middle of the road is a legitimate place to meet someone.

critique.note: Title is flat and factual in the right way, and "the stop that has nothing to do with exercise" is the whole flirt.

spaces.title: Harlem Week, All Free

spaceQuestion.text: Harlem Week is free all week — what are you actually showing up to, and who have you failed to drag along three years running?

spaces.whyNow: Harlem Week just kicked off with free concerts, outdoor movies, and a full block of programming that costs nothing to say yes to.

critique.note: "Stacked" is trying too hard. Trimmed to the part people actually answer.
critique.originalQuestion: Harlem Week is stacked and free — which one thing are you actually showing up to, and who in your life have you failed to drag to it three years running?

spaces.title: Aaliyah at the Bandshell

spaceQuestion.text: One in a Million comes on at the Bandshell on Saturday — which Aaliyah song ruins you a little, and what were you doing the first time you heard it?

spaces.whyNow: BRIC is throwing a free Aaliyah tribute at the Prospect Park Bandshell this Saturday, which means a few thousand Brooklynites are about to get emotional in the same field.

critique.note: Specific, emotional, and dated to a real Saturday. "Ruins you a little" is exactly the register.

spaces.title: Bleacher Seats, Cardinals

spaceQuestion.text: Sell me on your ballpark ritual — the seat, the beer, the inning you always leave by — and why you're right about all three.

spaces.whyNow: The Cardinals are at Yankee Stadium tonight with the Yanks holding a comfortable division lead, so the Bronx is loud and cheap seats are still findable.

critique.note: Question was a three-part form. One ritual, one opinion — easier to answer, funnier to argue with.
critique.originalQuestion: Yankees are up on the Cardinals tonight — sell me on your ballpark ritual: the seat, the beer, the inning you always leave by, and why you're right about all three.

spaces.title: The Most You've Paid For A Drink

spaceQuestion.text: A new Union Square bar put nearly everything under $11. So: what's the most you've ever paid for a drink, and were you showing off?

spaces.whyNow: Bernie and Herb's opened this week in the old Union Square coffee shop space with most drinks under $11, which in 2026 Manhattan qualifies as breaking news.

critique.note: Title was a price tag. The bar is just the excuse; the real question is the dumb expensive drink.
critique.originalQuestion: A new Union Square bar just put nearly everything under $11 — what's the most you've ever paid for a drink, and was it worth it or were you just showing off?

spaces.title: Runs That Aren't About Running

spaceQuestion.text: What's the thought you only ever finish thinking somewhere around mile three, and where in the city are you usually standing when it lands?

spaces.whyNow: For people whose real relationship with this city happens at 7am on a bridge or a loop, not at a bar.

critique.note: Title undercuts the fitness-post cliché, and "mile three" gives runners something real to confess.

spaces.title: Your 3AM Rewatch

spaceQuestion.text: Name the movie you've rewatched so many times you fall asleep to it — then tell me the exact scene you always wake up for.

spaces.whyNow: For the people who live alone in a small apartment and have one film doing quiet emotional maintenance in the background.

critique.note: The wake-up-for scene is a great tell — it turns a list answer into a small confession.
